findings.reason: Verified: processes come from get_context('spawn').Process, so they are SpawnProcess, a sibling of multiprocessing.Process under BaseProcess; the isinstance check is always False, kill() never runs (the old code killed every time), and a hang restart leaves duplicate flushers on the same shards sharing the same Values.

Verified in buffer.py:382-412 that max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)) per buffer, so splitting shards across P buffers multiplies the total flush budget and the per-shard backpressure threshold by P; a real but non-blocking change in what the option means.
Correct: get_memory_info calls iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client) on the same Redis client in every buffer, so the INFO requests repeat P times with the same ratio; a minor perf issue only.
Correct: the test patches time.sleep to a no-op, so the added time.sleep(0.1) does nothing and its comment is misleading; test cleanliness only.

Correct that no test covers restarting one of several processes; such a test would only catch the isinstance bug if it used real spawn processes, while the test suite uses threads via produce_to_pipe.
Correct: the docstring says one process per shard, but the count is min(max_processes, shards) and the CLI default is 1; a docs-only issue.
Verified with grep that _create_process_for_shard has no callers, and the `if not process` guard cannot skip because Process and Thread objects are always truthy; dead-code cleanup.
Correct: wait_produce uses the tag key 'shards' while the other metrics use 'shard', and the values differ in format; a naming inconsistency.
